title: observability: propagate request_id & traceparent, structured logs, per-endpoint metrics tags, streaming stability (OpenAI-compat)
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation:
This PR improves observability across the public API surface and the OpenAI-compat proxy by consistently propagating request identifiers and W3C trace context, emitting structured logs (JSON) with request_id/trace fields, and tagging per-endpoint metrics so we can slice latency/cost by route. While working on streaming stability for the OpenAI compatibility layer, we tightened up instrumentation so in-flight streaming responses include the same request/trace metadata and added defensive guards to avoid leaking internal IDs during retries/fallbacks.

What this changes (high level):
- Propagate X-Request-Id and W3C traceparent through gateway -> service -> streamer stack.
- Add middleware that normalizes/creates request_id and injects traceparent if missing.
- Structured (JSON) log formatter for API request lifecycle logs that include request_id, trace_id, span_id, route, and user/project identifiers where available.
- Per-endpoint metric tags: route, model_family, compat_mode. These tags are applied at the ingestion point so metrics backends (Prom, StatsD) can aggregate correctly.
- Streaming layer updates: ensure streaming chunks carry metadata (request_id, traceparent) for downstream logging/alerts; add idempotency guards to prevent duplicate logs on reconnect.
- OpenAI-compat proxy changes: preserve function-calling metadata while maintaining new observability fields and compatibility for existing clients.

Checklist:
- [x] Middleware to normalize request_id and traceparent
- [x] Structured log formatter + tests
- [x] Metric tags instrumentation and helper util
- [x] Streaming metadata propagation + stability fixes
- [x] OpenAI-compat proxy compatibility tests
- [x] Integration tests covering a canary route and fallbacks
- [x] Docs update (observability/README and OpenAI-compat notes)

Related tickets:
- ENG-3482 (observability: request/trace propagation)
- ENG-3550 (openai-compat: streaming stability and function-calling metadata)
- SUP-912 (customer report: missing request_id in logs during streaming reconnects)

Commits (summary):
- Normalize request id + add traceparent middleware
- Add structured-json log formatter for API request lifecycle
- Tag per-endpoint metrics at ingestion point
- Carry metadata in streaming chunks and add reconnect guards
- OpenAI-compat proxy: preserve function-calling metadata and add observability headers
- Tests: unit + integration + docs updates

Files changed (high level):
- redwood/api/middleware/observability.py (new middleware, request id & trace propagation)
- redwood/serve/streaming/streamer.py (propagate metadata with streaming chunks, reconnect guards)
- redwood/openai_compat/proxy.py (preserve metadata and compat adjustments)
- redwood/observability/logging/json_formatter.py (structured JSON formatter)
- redwood/console/metrics/tags.py (helper for per-endpoint tags)
- redwood-docs/observability/README.md (docs on request_id/trace usage)
- redwood-docs/openai-compat.md (compat notes and migration guidance)
- tests/integration/test-observability.py (integration tests for propagation and metrics tagging)
- ci/ci-pipelines.yml (add canary integration job)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Liam Chen (review): "Overall looks good. Two asks: 1) ensure the log formatter has a stable schema version field so downstream parsers can evolve; 2) add a short-lived feature flag for the per-endpoint tagger so we can roll this on a subset of traffic."
- Author (Ava): "Added schema_version to the formatter and the ff gate for metrics tagging. Default is off for a week so we can monitor canary."
- Priya Nair (review): "Streaming change: on reconnect we saw duplicate final chunk logs in the integration test, can you add idempotency token so we don't double-count?"
- Author: "Added idempotency_token to streaming chunk metadata and a guard in streamer to dedupe logs on reconnect."
- Ethan Brooks (security review): "Make sure we redact internal IDs and only emit project/user IDs when the request is authorized. Also validate incoming traceparent."
- Author: "Added redaction rules and strict traceparent parsing that falls back to generating a new trace if validation fails."

CI checks and timeline:
- Initial CI (lint/test/build): failed on import ordering and a flaky integration test (test_stream_reconnect).
- Fix 1 (2026-02-24): reorder imports and add idempotency token; lint now passes.
- Re-run CI: flaky integration test still failed intermittently; added a stronger wait/retry in test harness.
- Final CI run (2026-02-27): all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e canary job).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Deployed as a canary on a single region with metrics tagging disabled by default.
- Observability dashboards added: request_id distribution, per-route p50/p95 latency with new tags, streaming reconnect rate.
- Monitoring alert: spike in duplicate final-chunk logs => will auto-disable feature flag if observed.

Docs and migration notes:
- OpenAI-compat: clients should continue to work. We recommend passing their own X-Request-Id if they want to correlate logs. The proxy will preserve function-calling metadata and attach observability headers for our internal tracing.
- Added section in docs for how to query logs by request_id and trace_id and an example Grafana panel for per-route metrics.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers Liam Chen, Priya Nair, and Ethan Brooks.
- Merged by maintainer (squash) after CI green on 2026-02-28.

Notes/Follow-ups:
- ENG-3601 planned to wire trace spans into distributed sampling and to backfill trace linking in metrics.
- Keep an eye on downstream log ingestion costs after enabling structured logs (we included a schema_version and a compact set of fields to limit cardinality).
